sections.overview: The Sacred Kingfisher is a woodland kingfisher occurring in Australia and nearby western Pacific islands.
sections.identification: It has a turquoise back, buff-white underparts, a cream collar and a dark stripe through the eye.
sections.habitat: It uses open woodland, eucalyptus and paperbark forest, and mangroves.
sections.diet: It hunts mainly on land for insects, crustaceans and small reptiles, and only occasionally catches fish.
sections.behavior: It watches from an exposed perch, then swoops down and returns to the perch with its prey.
sections.reproduction: Both sexes excavate a nest burrow in a termite mound, hollow branch or river bank and share incubation and care of the young.
sections.ecology: In southeast Sulawesi it is a seasonal migrant that overwinters there, unlike the resident Collared Kingfisher.
sections.conservation: The 2016 global IUCN assessment lists the species as Least Concern.
